_meta.description: Suburban-SOC Agent Orchestration Checkpoints. Stores phase transitions (PENDING_APPROVAL, EXECUTED) to enable idempotency and crash recovery for the agent loop, keyed by alert_id (checkpoints.py does upsert-by-id GET/PUT plus an op_type=create claim doc). #245: NOT a data stream - a data stream only accepts op_type=create writes and has no GET-by-id, which write_checkpoint()/read_checkpoint() both need. No ILM policy: ILM ages out whole indices, not individual documents, and agent-checkpoints-<tenant> is a single always-growing index keyed by alert_id, not time-series data - retention needs a per-document TTL mechanism (tracked separately, see the compact_agent_approval_queue.py precedent for the same class of problem). #220: host/technique/last_seen/first_seen/suppressed_count/max_severity back should_suppress_technique()'s bounded sliding suppression-window docs (doc id "suppress:<sha256(host|technique)>", same index, different id shape from a bare alert_id or an "<alert_id>.claim" claim doc) - dynamic is strict, so these were added deliberately rather than left to fail every write with strict_dynamic_mapping_exception (caught in code review before this ever hit a real cluster: the fail-open error handling in agent.py would have silently absorbed that exception forever, making the whole feature a permanent no-op). last_seen/first_seen are `double`, not `date`: the code writes raw time.time() (float epoch-seconds), which is neither valid ISO date text nor valid epoch_millis (an integer). #276: resolved_by/resolved_at/resolution_reason/resolution_source/resolution_actor_claimed are set ONLY when a claim's RELEASED/RESOLVED transition came from manage_stuck_claims.py's manual recovery path (checkpoints._transition_claim's actor/reason kwargs) - the agent's own execute_approved()-driven transitions leave all five unset, same dynamic:strict reasoning as #220's fields above. resolved_by is the authenticated ES credential plus the OS user/host that ran the CLI (not attacker-controllable); resolution_actor_claimed is the operator's self-reported --actor value, a label only, same untrusted-claim shape as app.py's upstream_approver_claimed (security-auditor round-2: a free-text actor field alone would let anyone holding the credential forge attribution). A template PUT only shapes indices created AFTER it lands - configs/elasticsearch/apply-templates.sh separately PUTs these five properties directly to agent-checkpoints-*/_mapping so a pre-existing tenant index (dynamic:strict) doesn't reject the write.
